title: backup-progress.v1
description: A connector saying which stage of a backup it has reached. Deliberately almost empty. The temptation with a progress report is to attach what is being worked on - a file, a size, a table count - and every one of those would be a description of the site's data travelling under a heading that looks harmless. This carries a job identifier, a stage name from a closed list, and a timestamp. A stage is a claim about the site's own state, not a fact the platform can verify, and nothing decides anything on it.

stage.description: Enumerated so the set cannot grow by accident. Only 'dump' is sent today: it is the longest phase and the only one where the information is not derivable from a later report. The other two are reserved so a connector can begin sending them without a platform change.

at.description: Unix timestamp on the site's clock. Recorded alongside the platform's own, and ordered by the platform's, so a site with a wrong clock cannot reorder a timeline.
